title.en: Tie stride length to travelled distance

summary: Derive body speed from foot contact, or drive feet from body speed, but never let the two be authored independently.
objective: Make locomotion read as contact with the ground rather than as a sliding pose cycle.
applies_when: A character or creature walks, runs, crawls or climbs across a surface.
A looping locomotion clip is played while a controller moves the root.
Movement speed is variable, or the ground is uneven.
intent_signals: the walk looks like it is on ice
make the creature patrol the garden
example_prompts: Fix the sliding feet on the walking creature.
Let the creature slow down near the pond without the walk breaking.
negative_signals: Floating, hovering or swimming actors with no ground contact.
Deliberately weightless or dreamlike motion where sliding is the intent.
not_for: Floating, hovering or swimming actors with no ground contact.
Deliberately weightless or dreamlike motion where sliding is the intent.

principles: During a plant, the contact point should not move relative to the ground. Body displacement over one cycle therefore equals the stride the animation actually produces; if the controller speed and the clip disagree, the difference shows up as sliding.
There are two consistent architectures: motion extracted from the animation drives the body, or the body speed scales the playback rate of the cycle. Mixing them arbitrarily is what produces skate.
Uneven ground adds a second requirement: the planted foot must follow the surface height, otherwise the character floats on slopes and sinks on rises even when the horizontal speed is right.
Turning is part of the same budget. A body that rotates faster than the feet can step reads as a pivoting statue.
implementation: Pick the authority: extract root displacement from the clip for authored gaits, or measure the cycle stride once and scale playback by the current speed for procedural control.
Blend between separate cycles at their natural speeds rather than stretching one clip across an implausible range.
Add a per-foot adjustment against the ground query for slopes and steps, and keep it small so it corrects rather than replaces the animation.
Constrain turn rate and add lean or a step-turn transition so heading changes cost time.
Give creatures rests, glances and speed changes rather than a constant loop; irregularity should come from the state machine, not from noise on the transform.
observable_checks: Watch a single foot from a low camera through one full cycle: a planted foot that drifts backwards or forwards is skating.
Halve and double the movement speed and watch whether the cycle rate follows.
Walk across a slope and a step; the planted foot should stay in contact instead of hovering or penetrating.
Stop the actor abruptly: the pose should settle into a stance rather than freezing mid-stride.

creative_affordances: Stylised gaits, exaggerated hops and impossible creatures remain fully available; the constraint is between contact and displacement, not a realism requirement.
Deliberate skating, such as a skid into a turn, is expressive when it is authored rather than accidental.
known_limits: Authored motion guidance; no clip, controller or rendered gait has been measured for this record.
Clip playback alone does not provide obstacle avoidance, support or contact response; those need a separate model.
